nodes.question: A child or adolescent with a suspected soft tissue sarcoma. What is actually in this patient's file?
nodes.hint: Pick the highest tier of evidence genuinely in the file. A histology report is the usual basis for a soft tissue sarcoma code. Without one, only a few codes can be registered at all.
nodes.coding_note: Contract §4. Five routes, the Group 6 rn_document_inventory idiom. The inadequate-specimen route goes to st_imaging_report because an uninterpretable test drops to the nearest code (ruling 11). Cytology is captured as 'Cytology' in evidence_tests, as Groups 5 and 6 do.

options.label: Referral letter or clinical note only — no imaging report, no cytology, no histology report in the file
Ultrasound, CT or MRI report — no cytology or histology in the file
Fine-needle aspiration or other cytology report only — no histology report
Histology report from a biopsy or a resection
A specimen was taken but the report calls it inadequate, non-diagnostic or uninterpretable

nodes.question: What does the referral letter or clinical note say?
nodes.hint: Only one soft tissue sarcoma can be registered from a clinical note alone: Kaposi sarcoma of the skin, recognised on examination. Everything else needs at least an imaging report.
nodes.coding_note: Contract §0.7. Visser O, et al. Frontiers in Oncology 2023;13:1250549, Table 3, p. 04: Kaposi sarcoma of the skin is basis 1 at C44, 9140/3; sarcoma, NOS is basis 2, so a clinical note naming a sarcoma registers 8000/3 under rule 5, which ICCC-3 files in Group XII. Nodal, mucosal or visceral Kaposi sarcoma has no Table 3 row. check_group9_basis_rows requires the basis-1 branch to capture lesion_site 'skin'.

options.label: Kaposi sarcoma recognised on examination from skin lesions (purple or brown patches, plaques or nodules), with or without other sites involved
options.reason: Kaposi sarcoma of the skin may be registered on clinical examination alone, at basis 1 (Visser O, et al. Frontiers in Oncology 2023;13:1250549, Table 3, p. 04). Record the topography as the skin site of the lesions. A biopsy with HHV-8 (LANA-1) immunohistochemistry would confirm it.
options.upgrade_path: A biopsy with HHV-8 (LANA-1) immunohistochemistry would confirm Kaposi sarcoma. It would not change the code.

options.label: Kaposi sarcoma suspected with no skin lesions — lymph nodes, mouth or internal organs only
options.reason: The clinical exception covers Kaposi sarcoma of the skin only (Visser O, et al. Frontiers in Oncology 2023;13:1250549, Table 3, p. 04). Without pathology a nodal, mucosal or visceral Kaposi sarcoma is recorded as Neoplasm, malignant (8000/3) under rule 5, which ICCC-3 files in Group XII. A biopsy would register it as Kaposi sarcoma.

options.label: The note states or strongly suspects a soft tissue sarcoma or another malignant tumour, with no imaging and no pathology in the file
options.reason: A clinical note alone cannot register a sarcoma code: Visser O, et al. Frontiers in Oncology 2023;13:1250549, Table 3 gives sarcoma, NOS basis 2, which needs a clinical investigation such as imaging. Without pathology, and without a clinical investigation naming a sarcoma, the case is recorded as Neoplasm, malignant (8000/3) under Visser O, et al. Frontiers in Oncology 2023;13:1250549 rule 5 (p. 03). ICCC-3 files 8000/3 at a soft tissue site in Group XII.

options.label: The note describes a lump or swelling that a benign process could equally explain — lipoma, haemangioma, abscess, reactive lymph node
options.reason: A benign process could equally explain this. Under Visser O, et al. Frontiers in Oncology 2023;13:1250549 rule 4 (p. 03), a case where malignancy is only possible is not registered without pathology.

nodes.question: What does the imaging report conclude?
nodes.hint: Code from the radiologist's stated conclusion. Imaging can register only four soft tissue codes, each only when the report names that diagnosis as likely. A biopsy sets every other soft tissue sarcoma code.
nodes.coding_note: Contract §0.7. Visser O, et al. Frontiers in Oncology 2023;13:1250549, Table 3, p. 04: sarcoma NOS 8800/3, liposarcoma 8850/3, leiomyosarcoma 8890/3 and angiosarcoma 9120/3 at basis 2, any site. The pathway's §2B ('never an entity code') is half right: 8800/3 is itself a Table 3 code. Rule 4 governs the benign and indeterminate option. Registrar questions F asks whether the three subtype codes should stay for a paediatric population.

options.reason: Imaging that names a sarcoma as likely registers Sarcoma, NOS (8800/3) at basis 2 (Visser O, et al. Frontiers in Oncology 2023;13:1250549, Table 3, p. 04). A sarcoma type other than liposarcoma, leiomyosarcoma or angiosarcoma has no imaging row of its own, so it is recorded as Sarcoma, NOS until a biopsy names it.

options.reason: Liposarcoma named on imaging registers Liposarcoma, NOS (8850/3) at basis 2 (Visser O, et al. Frontiers in Oncology 2023;13:1250549, Table 3, p. 04). The subtype needs a biopsy.

options.label: Leiomyosarcoma named as the likely diagnosis
options.reason: Leiomyosarcoma named on imaging registers Leiomyosarcoma, NOS (8890/3) at basis 2 (Visser O, et al. Frontiers in Oncology 2023;13:1250549, Table 3, p. 04).

options.label: Angiosarcoma named as the likely diagnosis
options.reason: Angiosarcoma named on imaging registers Hemangiosarcoma (9120/3) at basis 2 (Visser O, et al. Frontiers in Oncology 2023;13:1250549, Table 3, p. 04).

options.label: A malignant tumour is likely, but the report does not say it is a sarcoma

options.label: The lesion arises in bone
options.reason: A tumour arising in bone is ICCC-3 Group VIII, not a soft tissue sarcoma. Osteosarcoma and chondrosarcoma have their own imaging rows at C40-C41 (Visser O, et al. Frontiers in Oncology 2023;13:1250549, Table 3).

options.label: Benign or indeterminate — lipoma, haemangioma, vascular or lymphatic malformation, haematoma, abscess, or malignancy described only as possible
options.reason: A benign process could equally explain this. Under Visser O, et al. Frontiers in Oncology 2023;13:1250549 rule 4 (p. 03), a case where malignancy is only possible is not registered without pathology.

nodes.question: What does the cytology report conclude?
nodes.hint: Cytology cannot establish most soft tissue sarcoma types. Record the line it names and no more; a biopsy sets the type.

A malignant small round cell tumour whose lineage the cytology does not establish is not yet a sarcoma and goes to Group XII as 8002/3. A non-diagnostic specimen drops to the imaging conclusion (ruling 11).

nodes.question: Besides the routine histology, what does the pathology file contain?
nodes.hint: Choose a molecular option only when a FISH, RT-PCR or sequencing report identifies the fusion or rearrangement that defines the tumour the report names — for example EWSR1::FLI1 in Ewing sarcoma, SS18::SSX in synovial sarcoma, PAX3::FOXO1 in alveolar rhabdomyosarcoma, ETV6::NTRK3 in infantile fibrosarcoma, EWSR1::WT1 in desmoplastic small round cell tumour, ASPSCR1::TFE3 in alveolar soft part sarcoma. A mutation or copy-number change that does not define the tumour does not count.

Frontiers in Oncology 2023;13:1250549, rule 10, p. 06). Every named-diagnosis branch below asserts 7; basisOfDiagnosis() takes the highest.

nodes.question: Record each stain as the report states it.
nodes.hint: CD99 alone does not establish Ewing sarcoma: lymphoblastic lymphoma, synovial sarcoma, desmoplastic small round cell tumour and some rhabdomyosarcomas also stain for it. nodes.coding_note: The pathway's §2E fork 1 and §4C panel (Sbaraglia M, Dei Tos AP, et al. Virchows Archiv 2019; Thway K, Fisher C. Surgical Pathology Clinics 2023; Thway K. International Journal of Surgical Pathology 2016). Non-sarcoma exits first: CD45 and TdT to Group II (lymphoblastic lymphoma is CD99-positive), PHOX2B to Group IV. Myogenin goes to the rhabdomyosarcoma type question. BCOR is not a rule: its outcome equals the fallback, so it could never change the code.

resolution_logic.reason: CD45 (leucocyte common antigen) marks a lymphoma, not a sarcoma. Lymphoma is ICCC-3 Group II.
TdT marks lymphoblastic lymphoma, which is also CD99-positive and is the classic mimic of Ewing sarcoma. Lymphoblastic lymphoma is ICCC-3 Group II.
PHOX2B marks neuroblastoma, which is ICCC-3 Group IV.
Myogenin marks skeletal muscle differentiation: this is a rhabdomyosarcoma. The next screen asks for the type.
Desmin, cytokeratin and WT1 together are the polyphenotypic pattern of desmoplastic small round cell tumour (8806/3).
SS18-SSX fusion-specific staining identifies synovial sarcoma, here the poorly differentiated round cell form. Recorded as Synovial sarcoma, NOS (9040/3).

Membranous CD99 with nuclear NKX2.2 identifies Ewing sarcoma. Ewing sarcoma is 9364/3 in ICD-O-3.2. The number 9260/3 that older lists and the REDCap dropdown still show was retired in ICD-O-3.2 and now belongs to a benign bone cyst.

Surgical Pathology Clinics 2018, PDF p. 1, gives loss in 34-73% of MPNST and in 'a minority of synovial sarcomas, fibrosarcomatous dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans, and melanoma'; the pathway pairs it with the nerve sheath context. resolution_logic.reason: HHV-8 (LANA-1) nuclear staining in a spindle cell lesion identifies Kaposi sarcoma (9140/3).
Myogenin in a spindle cell sarcoma marks spindle cell rhabdomyosarcoma (8912/3).
SS18-SSX fusion-specific staining identifies synovial sarcoma; in a spindle cell tumour, Synovial sarcoma, spindle cell (9041/3).
Pan-TRK staining in a spindle cell tumour of a child under 2 supports infantile fibrosarcoma (8814/3). ETV6::NTRK3 would confirm it.
Loss of H3K27me3 in a spindle cell tumour with nerve sheath features supports a malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumour (9540/3).
Nuclear STAT6 identifies a solitary fibrous tumour. The next screen asks whether the report calls it malignant.
MUC4 marks low-grade fibromyxoid sarcoma and sclerosing epithelioid fibrosarcoma, both coded under Myxosarcoma (8840/3).
Desmin with h-caldesmon marks smooth muscle differentiation: Leiomyosarcoma, NOS (8890/3).
